blocks.title: Instantaneous and average rate
blocks.text: The rate at any one instant during an interval is the instantaneous rate. The average rate of reaction is the rate between two specific times, the rate over a time period.
The average and instantaneous rates are equal at only one instant in any interval: at first the instantaneous rate is higher than the average, and at the end of the interval it is lower.

blocks.caption: Sample Problem 7.1: ammonia in the Haber process, N2 + 3H2 gives 2NH3
rows: Instantaneous rate after 1.0 min (delta C = 2.7 mol dm-3 in 1 min, as printed)
Average rate between 1.0 and 4.0 min, [NH3] 3.5 then 6.2 mol dm-3

blocks.prompt: Why does the instantaneous rate change during a reaction, and when is it equal to the average rate?
blocks.explanation: The rate depends on the concentrations of the reactants, which fall continuously as they are used up, so the slope of the curve, the instantaneous rate, falls from moment to moment. Over any interval it starts above the average and ends below it, matching the average at exactly one instant in between.

items: Instantaneous rate: the slope at one instant; average rate: the change over an interval (Haber sample: 2.7 mol dm-3 over 3.0 min = 0.90 mol dm-3 min-1); they coincide at one instant only.
